jobs.jd: NVIDIA has helped redefine what computers can do. Now, generative AI is opening new possibilities for how people learn, create, and tackle problems. Realizing that potential means answering some of the hardest questions in AI: Where do models fall short? Which risks are we missing? How do we know our safeguards are working? As an expert in machine learning for Evaluations, you’ll help establish the evidence that guides the next generation of safer AI. Your curiosity and scientific judgment can shape what we test, what we learn, and what we build next. We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer / AI Researcher / Data Scientist to join our AI Safety and Responsibility efforts within Enterprise Risk Management. Engaging directly in engineering tasks, you will apply your data science and statistics skills. You will turn open research questions into rigorous benchmarks, inventive experiments, and tools that reveal how multimodal large language models behave under pressure. Working with researchers and platform engineers, you’ll connect those discoveries to better training methods and safeguards, with reproducible results that inform technical reviews and executive decisions. If you love asking the question no one has thought to test, and building a convincing way to answer it, come help us define what progress in AI safety looks like. What You Will Be Doing: Safety Benchmarking: Design and maintain safety benchmarks for large language and multimodal models, translating risk scenarios into test cases, datasets, and scoring rubrics. Evaluation Methodology: Define metrics and protocols that assess safety alongside model usefulness, using baselines, uncertainty estimates, and failure analysis to distinguish meaningful improvements from noise. Reproducible Evaluation: Build reusable Python pipelines with versioned datasets, model configurations, and experiment tracking to reproduce results and compare performance across model releases. Automated Red-Teaming: Develop tools to discover failure modes and expand evaluation coverage, incorporating human review to validate automated scoring and provide additional judgment. Failure Analysis: Investigate model failures with researchers, document actionable findings, and develop regression tests to assess whether model changes resolve identified issues. Results and Communication: Partner with platform engineers to store and aggregate evaluation results, and clearly communicate findings, limitations, and emerging risks to researchers and decision-makers. What We Need To See: Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, with 6+ years in the field of machine learning engineering or evaluation. Evaluation Design: Experience developing benchmarks, metrics, and statistically sound comparisons for ML systems, including selecting baselines and interpreting uncertainty. Ability to translate ambiguous evaluation questions into testable experiments. Engineering: Strong Python skills and experience building maintainable shared tools, data pipelines, and experiment-tracking workflows. Analytical Rigor: Ability to assess dataset quality, identify limitations in metrics and scoring methods, and support conclusions with reproducible evidence. Communication: Clearly explain findings and tradeoffs to researchers, engineering partners, and executives. Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd: Evaluation: Experience evaluating LLMs, multimodal models, or agentic systems through adversarial testing or automated red-teaming. Community Contributions: Contributions to public benchmarks or evaluation frameworks. Research Publications: A publication track record and interest in continuing to publish at top tier venues. Human-Aligned Evaluation: Experience validating model-based evaluators against human judgments or designing human-in-the-loop evaluation workflows. Statistical Rigor: Strong model evaluation skills and a commitment to sound statistical practices, including confidence intervals. Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are: 187,500 USD – 364,000 USD for Level 4; and 232,500 USD – 442,000 USD for Level 5. You will also be eligible for equity and benefits . Job Description The AI Engineer designs, deploys, and maintains on-premises AI solutions that process healthcare documents at scale. This role owns the end-to-end pipeline, from hosting and operating locally deployed large language models, to ingesting and extracting text from document images (PDF and TIFF), to engineering and refining prompts, to validating results and writing structured output to SQL Server. Location: Remote ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS: Deploy, configure, and maintain locally hosted large language models, including the supporting GPU/server infrastructure, inference serving, and model version management. Evaluate, benchmark, and recommend new or updated on-premises models as the technology evolves. Build and maintain automated pipelines that retrieve documents (PDF, TIFF) from network shares and perform OCR and text extraction. Design, test, and iteratively refine prompts and structured-output logic to improve accuracy, consistency, and reliability for each project. Validate AI output programmatically and write results to SQL Server, ensuring data integrity and traceability. Compile and deliver results to CQA for audit; analyze CQA findings to determine what should change in prompts, extraction, or model configuration. Manage multiple concurrent AI projects in collaboration with the PMO, maintaining test sets, accuracy metrics, and version history of prompts and workflows. Partner with Cybersecurity and Compliance to ensure on-premises AI systems, data handling, and access controls meet HIPAA, data-governance, and organizational security requirements. Maintain documentation of architectures, workflows, test results, and configurations. Stay current with developments in open-weight language models, OCR/document AI, and model-serving technology. Perform other duties as assigned to advance the organization’s AI strategy and innovation initiatives. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES: Strong understanding of large language models, including the practical limits of locally hosted models (context size, quantization, throughput, hardware requirements). Proficiency in Python for pipeline development, automation, and data handling. Experience deploying and operating models in a self-hosted environment, including GPU infrastructure, inference serving, and Linux or Windows server administration. Working knowledge of SQL Server, including writing and troubleshooting queries and inserts (AI-assisted proficiency acceptable). Experience with OCR and document-processing workflows for scanned or image-based documents (PDF, TIFF). Strong prompt-engineering skills, including structured/JSON output design and systematic accuracy testing. Ability to measure and communicate model accuracy using test sets, metrics, and reviewer feedback. Familiarity with HIPAA, data privacy, and security principles related to AI and PHI. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work with clinical, technical, and non-technical stakeholders. Ability to manage multiple projects with strong documentation habits and attention to detail. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems, or a related field preferred, or equivalent experience. 1+ years of experience deploying or working with language models, NLP, or automation systems. jobs.jd: If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/ About Us Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day. We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process. About the Role We're looking for a data scientist with strong statistics and modeling skills to be the science partner for the machine learning and recommendation systems behind Twitch's discovery products. You will work with product managers, ML engineers and applied scientists to help build what our recommendation systems should optimize for. That means balancing what a viewer does today (a click, a play, minutes watched) against what keeps them coming back: return visits, daily habits, and lasting connections with creators. It also means weighing short-form clips against long-form live content, and each surface against the others. This role will draw from a variety of statistical learning techniques, causal inference, optimization and recommender systems evaluation, and it still owns the full path from question to decision. Reporting to the Director of Data Science, you will work from our San Francisco, CA office. You Will - Help define the objective functions and success metrics for ranking and recommendations across feeds, search and notifications. Make the trade-offs explicit between short-term engagement (clicks, plays, watch time) and long-term outcomes (return visits, retention, new creator connections), including how short-form clips and live content add to or take away from each other. - Evaluate ranking, recommendation and feed changes with ML engineers and applied scientists. This covers A/B tests and long-running holdouts, offline metrics that predict online results, and the cost and value of exploration and cold start. Handle the hard cases: novelty effects, interference between experiments, two-sided marketplace effects involving creators and viewers, and feedback loops in recommendation data. - Build statistical and ML models that explain viewer behavior and size opportunities, such as propensity, uplift, survival and retention models. Include proxy metrics that predict long-term retention, so teams can decide in days rather than months. - Turn ambiguous product questions into clear analyses. Quantify the uncertainty, and make recommendations that inform the machine learning and discovery roadmap. - Define the logging and data needed to measure discovery surfaces, and check its quality. - Contribute to the team's standards for experimentation, causal inference and model evaluation, and share what you learn with other data scientists. Perks - Medical, Dental, Vision & Disability Insurance - 401(k) - Maternity & Parental Leave - Flexible PTO - Amazon Employee Discount About the team Twitch is all about community, and our Community team is a core pillar of what makes Twitch, Twitch. Community Discovery & ML (CDML) helps millions of viewers find the creators and communities they'll love. That covers search, browse, the mobile live and clips feeds, recommended notifications, and the recommendation systems behind them. When a viewer finds a new creator through one of these, it's often the start of a lasting connection. That connection is what keeps viewers, and the creators they watch, coming back. - 3+ years of data scientist experience - A BA/BS in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Science or a related quantitative field, or equivalent industry experience. - 3+ years as a data scientist in a high-velocity, data-driven environment, with hands-on experience applying statistical modeling and machine learning (regression, classification, causal inference, time series), including the assumptions behind each method and when it fails. - Experience designing and analyzing online experiments, including variance reduction, power analysis and the pitfalls of interpreting results. - Expert SQL and proficiency in Python or R. - A track record of using data and models to influence product decisions and leadership. - An MS or PhD in a quantitative field. - Experience with recommender systems, search ranking or feed ranking, such as offline evaluation (precision and recall, NDCG), exploration versus exploitation, or cold-start problems. - Experience with multi-objective optimization or with defining objective functions for ranking systems, including choosing weights between competing goals. - Experience building proxy metrics for long-term outcomes, or estimating long-term effects from long-running holdouts or observational data (e.g., difference-in-differences, synthetic control, uplift modeling). - Experience with two-sided platforms or marketplaces, where changes for viewers also affect creators or supply. - Experience on a consumer content platform: streaming, short-form video, social or marketplaces. - Familiarity with Twitch, as a viewer or a creator (or both!). jobs.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Post-Training — Collective Alignment (User Signals)
jobs.jd: About the Team The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT. Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. Our team develops scientific approaches to understanding these signals and translating them into improvements in model behavior through evaluations, reward modeling, and post-training. About the Role As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time. You will develop new approaches to extracting meaningful learning signals from complex user interactions and incorporating those signals into model training. This role requires strong deep learning research skills, scientific rigor, and curiosity about how people interact with AI. You will design controlled experiments and ablations, critically examine the relationship between offline evaluations and online model behavior, and work closely with research, product, and data science teams to understand whether improvements translate into meaningful value for users. In this role, you will: - Develop novel methods for learning from human feedback and user interaction signals. - Research approaches to incorporating feedback into reward modeling, reinforcement learning, and post-training. - Design rigorous experiments and ablation studies to isolate the effects of new data, objectives, and training methods. - Develop offline evaluations and investigate their relationship with online experiments and real-world user outcomes. - Analyze unexpected results, investigate discrepancies between evaluation metrics and user behavior, and develop hypotheses to guide further research. - Evaluate tradeoffs and regressions to improve targeted model behaviors while preserving broader capabilities. - Collaborate with research, alignment, product, and data science teams. - Implement and debug experiments across large-scale deep learning research systems. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have a strong background in deep learning research through academic or industry experience. - Have demonstrated research ability through publications or substantive research contributions in deep learning or LLM post-training. - Have experience developing new machine learning methods and evaluating them through rigorous, hypothesis-driven experimentation. - Think critically about experimental design, measurement, and what evaluation results do and do not establish about model behavior. - Are comfortable designing ablations, investigating surprising results, and reasoning about the relationship between offline metrics and real-world outcomes. - Have strong programming skills and experience working with complex ML codebases. - Are curious about how people interact with AI and how those interactions can inform better models. Nice to have: - Experience with RLHF, reinforcement learning, or modern LLM post-training. - Research or demonstrated interest in AI alignment, human feedback, or user signals. - Experience with online experimentation, evaluation methodology, or learning from noisy and biased feedback. - Experience connecting machine learning research with real-world product behavior. jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Alexa AI - ML Engineering
jobs.jd: Alexa Proactive, now powered by Alexa+, brings customers personalized, proactive content, suggestions and actions across Alexa devices and surfaces: news, sports, recipes, music, shopping deals and tips to discover new features. Behind these experiences are recommendation and ranking systems that anticipate what customers need and surface the right content, suggestions, or actions at the right moment, through the right channel. Deciding what to show, to whom, when, and through which channel, for millions of customers, is a large-scale recommendation and ranking problem, and much of its science is still ahead of us. We are looking for a Senior Applied Scientist to join ML Engineering (MLE) India in Bengaluru, part of the Personalization and Delivery Engineering (PDE) org in Alexa AI, and build the recommendation and ranking systems behind Alexa+ proactive experiences. You will be part of Proactive Science, a global science team across time zones, and set the scientific direction for your area: content retrieval and relevance, ranking and re-ranking, how the full page is composed, and how the system learns from customer feedback. You will work closely with Proactive Science partners and with the software and data engineers who run these systems in production. We value scientists who can move fast: iterate on algorithms quickly, validate ideas through rigorous online experiments, and turn them into measurable customer and business impact. As a senior scientist, you will frame ambiguous problems on your own, make sound trade-offs between model quality, latency and cost, and deliver end-to-end solutions to production with limited guidance. You will also mentor scientists and engineers, and influence engineering, product, and science partners across teams. Key job responsibilities - Science roadmap: Own the science roadmap for proactive recommendation and ranking. Turn customer and business goals into clear ML problems, plans and metrics. - Proactive recommendation and ranking: Design and scale multi-stage recommendation systems (candidate generation, relevance filtering, ranking, re-ranking, and delivery policy) that decide what to surface, to whom, when, and through which channel, for millions of customers across Alexa devices and surfaces. - Personalization: Move ranking from popularity to deep personalization, using customer interests, engagement history, context (time of day, device) and content understanding. Apply two-tower retrieval, cross-encoders, learning-to-rank, CTR/CVR prediction, and sequential and multi-task recommendation models. - Whole-page optimization: Optimize the whole page, not only the ranked list: slot rules, diversity, share of voice and backup content. - Objective design and alignment: Build multi-objective ranking and optimization frameworks that align model objectives with business goals and customer experience metrics, with guardrails against fatigue, dismissals and repeated content. - Rapid iteration to impact: Drive fast experimentation cycles from hypothesis to offline evaluation, online A/B testing, and launch. Continuously improve models based on customer feedback and online results. - Explore and exploit: Bring explore and exploit into the system through contextual bandits, counterfactual and off-policy evaluation. - ML foundations: Partner with software and data engineers to build a feature store shared by training and inference, feature data-quality checks, automated retraining with evaluation gates, and model performance dashboards (CTR, NDCG and business metrics). - Content understanding and generation: Use LLMs and embeddings to strengthen content understanding, topic tagging and representations for ranking, and contribute to the generation of proactive content. - Scientific rigor: Own the full science lifecycle with sound experiment design, counterfactual evaluation, and production accountability. Ship models within strict latency and cost budgets, with safe fallbacks (for example distillation and efficient inference). - Leadership: Mentor scientists and engineers, run science and design reviews, write clear documents for senior leaders, raise the hiring bar, and build reusable science components across teams. A day in the life A DAY IN THE LIFE No two days look the same, because many of the hardest problems are still open. You might start the morning with A/B results for a personalized re-ranker: clicks went up, but so did dismissals. You decide how to balance the two before you dial it up. Next, you take on a cold-start problem: a new content provider has no engagement history, so how should it earn a slot without hurting the page? With Proactive Science partners across time zones, you shape next half's roadmap: move from popularity ranking to deep personalization, replace fixed slot rules with a learned whole-page policy, add explore and exploit, and make retraining automatic. With software and data engineers, you work out how a larger model fits a tight latency budget, and what safe fallback serves when it times out. You end the day writing a short proposal that turns one open question into a plan the team can build. About the team ML Engineering (MLE) India, part of Personalization and Delivery Engineering (PDE) in Alexa AI, builds the personalization and proactive-intelligence systems that let Alexa anticipate what customers need before they ask. In Bengaluru, we own the AERO runtime, which selects and composes proactive content for Alexa devices, and CxT (Customer Experience Telemetry), which captures how customers see and engage with that content. Together with Proactive Science, our global science team, we turn this into better proactive experiences for customers. - Shape the science: you set the roadmap, pick the problems, and define how science and engineering work together on proactive experiences. - A direct path to customers: our team runs the system that serves your models, and our telemetry gives you the signals you learn from. jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Demand Tech, Amazon Ads
jobs.jd: In Amazon Advertising, we apply machine learning at massive scale to optimize the prediction, ranking, and bidding behind every ad - deciding, in milliseconds, which ads to show shoppers and how to value them. We're looking for an experienced Applied Scientist to lead a science area within how we rank, value, and bid on ads for Amazon DVA+ (Display, Video, and Audio) - including how we judge whether an ad is a good fit for the page a shopper is on and for the shopper themselves. It's high-scale, low-latency, customer-facing science: your models run live in front of millions of shoppers under tight real-time constraints. The questions are genuinely open - how do you tell whether an ad is relevant to someone, how do you balance what's good for shoppers, advertisers, and Amazon, and how do you keep getting that right as shopping behavior and inventory shift underneath you? You'll set the technical direction for how we answer them, and have room to shape where we take it. A few things make this stand out: your models touch a huge share of the ads shoppers see every day, so even small improvements add up fast; you'll run modern ML live under strict latency limits, across regions and very different types of ad inventory; and the problem space is rich - from how we value and bid on ads, to keeping models stable as traffic shifts, to what makes an ad a good fit for a shopper. Key job responsibilities - Be the scientific point of reference for your area, mentoring scientists and engineers and raising the team's bar through code, design, and science review. - Shape the science roadmap for your area, aligning partner teams and building consensus across science and business. - Advance the state of the art in ranking, deep learning, and information retrieval, judging which problems are genuinely new versus solvable with existing approaches, and set the standards the team builds on. - Own ambiguous problems end to end with limited guidance: frame them, break them down for yourself and others, prototype, experiment, and ship. - Define how the team weighs competing objectives — shopper experience, advertiser and publisher value, and Amazon's business — and the metrics that keep models holding up across placements and marketplaces. - Write and ship your own production code, moving fast with modern AI coding assistants and agents — we're all builders here. A day in the life You might start by digging into last week's experiment results, then use an AI coding agent to get your next prototype built and ready to test in production. In the afternoon you could be sketching a new way to measure ad relevance, reading a recent paper that bears on it, and reviewing a teammate's design - as you are the person the team turns to when a problem gets hard. You'll move between hands-on science, writing and shipping real production code, setting the direction for your area, and helping the scientists and engineers around you do their best work. jobs.title: Sr. Software Development Engineer – AI/ML Networking Disaggregated Inference, Annapurna Labs, Annapurna Labs
jobs.jd: Every token a large language model generates depends on data reaching the right accelerator at the right moment. As AI models outgrow any single chip, the network between accelerators becomes the bottleneck that decides how fast — and how affordably — the world's largest models can serve real users. That network layer is what our team builds. We're in search of an engineer to work at the frontier of disaggregated inference: splitting LLM serving into separate prefill and decode pools and moving the model's KV cache between them at the absolute limit of what the hardware allows. Get it right and users get answers in milliseconds; get it wrong and the fastest accelerators in the world sit idle waiting on data. You'll own pieces of the high-speed transfer path that make the difference, and you'll measure your success in how close you run to the theoretical peak of the machine. What we're looking for: Strong C/C++ and a love for low-level, performance-critical systems — solid command of Linux, kernels, memory, and writing fast code. The instinct to ask "how fast could this possibly go?" and the rigor to measure it. Experience with high-speed networking or HPC interconnects (RDMA, InfiniBand, libfabric, UCX, NIXL, MPI) is valued highly; embedded-systems experience is a plus. Prior AI/ML experience is welcome but not required — if you're a great systems engineer, we'll teach you the ML side. If you like solving genuinely hard problems, working shoulder-to-shoulder with HPC and ML customers, iterating fast, and shipping at a scale few places can offer, come join us. This is a role on the leading edge of AI/ML infrastructure. Key job responsibilities Build and optimize the low-level data-movement software across accelerators, servers, and heterogeneous memory — over AWS's highest-performance network fabric. Push performance to the hardware roofline: profile, find the real bottleneck, and close the gap between "it works" and "it runs as fast as physics permits." Work across the stack — from kernel and network transport up to the inference frameworks — and partner with teams building the chips, runtime, and models. Deliver features that run on our largest clusters, for our largest customers, serving the largest AI models in production. A day in the life Annapurna Labs, a crucial part of AWS, is responsible for developing hardware and software components for EC2 infrastructure. Our team focuses on building networking solutions that for Machine Learning (ML) and High-Performance Computing (HPC) workloads on AWS. We have mixed discipline orgs, you’d be working side by side with infrastructure experts, hardware engineers, RTL engineers, scientists & architects. Our workforce spans the globe and is truly international, you’ll find yourself working side by side with individuals from numerous countries. We take mentorship seriously, you can both expect senior mentorship and will be expected to mentor new and junior engineers. The pace is fast as we work on the latest advancements of AI/ML, but we take the time to bond as a team and enjoy the successes. jobs.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
jobs.jd: About the Team The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization. Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT. Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations. About the Role We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship. We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required. In this role, you will - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals. - Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models. - Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings. - Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss. - Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training. - Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute. - Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements. - Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users. You might thrive in this role if you - Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models. - Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit. - Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure. - Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems. - Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous. - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype. - Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem. If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. About the team

The Office of the Field CCO works with the Chief Marketing and Chief Revenue Officers of Databricks’ largest customers to redesign how their commercial organizations operate. We build a peer community of CMOs and CROs, partner with them on go-to-market transformation programs, and ensure those programs deliver measurable business results. The work cuts across sales, marketing, field engineering, and partner teams, and it runs on the customer’s own data.

About the role

You will help to shape and lead Databricks’ strategy for driving AI transformations with our customers. You will report directly to the Field CCO. 

This is a role with broad scope that will require you to collaborate across the business: you will set how we deliver transformation engagements, select and run our first 10 pilot accounts, and shape the reusable solutions field engineering builds. You will get work done through account teams, field engineering, field marketing, and enablement.

Shape the reusable solutions

Select and run the pilot program

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.jd:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Auterion, you will play a pivotal role in the successful development, integration and deployment of Auterion-powered drone systems. 

In this role, you will collaborate closely with the production, hardware engineering, and firmware/software teams, as well as operations, ensuring that every platform transitions smoothly from an airframe concept into a fully validated flying robot ready for deployment. You will serve as the primary technical interface for partners, work closely with them to understand their technical requirements, configure and adapt existing solutions, contribute to core software development, and ensure successful implementation. 

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys combining hands-on technical work with customer collaboration and system-level problem solving, bridging the gap between hardware, firmware, and real-world flight performance. 

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Operate in a highly hands-on environment with evolving system requirements, rapidly iterating across hardware and software integration challenges.
  • Manage software releases and perform firmware flashing and configuration using PX4 or adjacent autopilot ecosystems, including sensor calibration, ESC tuning, and system bring-up.
  • Provide deep avionics and airframe expertise, including autopilot tuning, sensor and payload integration, power systems and airworthiness considerations.
  • Work independently to troubleshoot integration and flight-readiness issues while collaborating cross-functionally with hardware engineering, firmware/software teams, operations, and QC engineering to escalate complex challenges when required.
  • Act as the primary technical authority in customer engagements, translating mission requirements into concrete system architectures and demonstrable solutions built on AuterionOS and Skynode.
  • Participate in flight testing activities to validate platform stability, safety, and mission performance, resolving technical issues often directly in the field during customer trials and demonstrations.
  • Contribute to technical documentation and continuous improvement of engineering processes.
  • Feed customer and market requirements back into product and engineering teams to influence the roadmap of the Auterion stack.

Qualifications and Skills

  • Degree in Software, Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace or Robotics Engineering, or a related field
  • Working proficiency in C/C++ and Python: you can read, debug and patch existing code and write small tools and scripts
  • Comfortable in Linux environments, including the command line, logs, Docker and basic networking (IP, TCP/UDP)
  • Hands-on hardware-software integration: system bring-up, wiring and connectors, and embedded interfaces (UART, CAN, I2C, SPI) at a practical level
  • Structured troubleshooting: you can isolate whether a problem is software, hardware, configuration or RF, often under time pressure in the field
  • Strong communicator: you can explain technical issues clearly to customers and operators, and report findings back to engineering in a way they can act on
  • Willing to travel and work on-site with customers, including at test ranges and in field environments
  • EU citizenship (required for security clearance and customer requirements)

Nice-to-have

  • Experience with PX4 or ArduPilot, MAVLink, QGroundControl or mission planning tools
  • UAV flight testing and validation in operational environments
  • Experience with datalinks and radio systems
  • Previous customer-facing or field engineering role, especially with defense or government customers
  • German language skills

Benefits

  • Flexible working hours
  • Stock Options
  • Generous holiday allowance
  • Pension plan 
  • Extended social security package 
  • Enhanced maternity & paternity leave

We are building the leading software platform for AI-powered autonomous systems for enterprise and government customers. Our team is supporting the most important missions and solving the most challenging problems.

At Auterion, we bring together the sharpest minds who love to solve the hardest problems. Join a vibrant team built on innovation, openness, and excellence, where you’ll be empowered to develop ideas, collaborate across all levels, and make an impact that matters.

jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Last Hundred Yards
jobs.jd: Every doorstep is different. Our robot has to understand all of them. We're building robots to deliver packages to customer homes. To make that possible, we're creating a system that can automatically generate a simulation-ready digital twin of the outdoor delivery environment for every customer home Amazon delivers to; modeling the driveways, yards, walkways, stairs, porches, and doorsteps a robot must understand and navigate. And the goal isn't simply to create virtual worlds that look real. They need to be real in the ways that matter to a robot. Geometry, semantics, appearance, physical properties, and the varied environmental cues that influence perception, planning, and motion, must be reproduced faithfully so robot behaviors from the field are repeatable in simulation. Our simulator becomes an effective tool to study the problem. The same autonomy software that runs on the physical robot also runs in simulation. When robot behavior differs between simulation and reality, we can ask why, and improve the representation, simulation, or models that produced the difference. Our North Star ambition is a system capable of modeling the delivery environment for every customer home we serve, across the enormous diversity of real residential environments. There isn't an established recipe for doing this. We are advancing the knowledge frontier of scene reconstruction. The right representation may combine classical geometry, learned scene representations, generative models, world models, or approaches that haven't been invented yet. We're interested in people with deep expertise in one or more areas of: Computer vision, 3D graphics, scene reconstruction, physics simulation, neural scene representations, Gaussian splatting, generative AI, world models, or related areas - with a strong interest in applying that expertise to robotics. Role Overview This is applied research with a short distance from idea conception to physical consequence. You'll work closely with robotics, autonomy, simulation, and software engineers to turn promising methods into systems that change how real robots perceive, plan, and navigate at Amazon scale. As a Sr. Applied Scientist on the Last Mile Robotics team, you will develop cutting-edge methods for capturing, reconstructing, and simulating real-world delivery environments in high-fidelity 3D. Your work will directly enable autonomous robots to understand and navigate the diverse conditions found at customer doorsteps. You will push the boundaries of scene reconstruction, neural rendering, and generative modeling, transforming scientific breakthroughs into physical impact through rapid experimentation and close collaboration with robotics, autonomy, and simulation teams. - Experience in applied research - Knowledge of programming languages such as C/C++, Python, Java or Perl Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.jd: About Agon Agon is building Europe’s defence AI lab. We develop the sovereign infrastructure and AI foundation models to train, test and evolve autonomous defence systems, in Europe and for Europe. At the heart of it is a synthetic battlefield: a virtual testing ground where drones, vessels and other autonomous systems face adaptive adversaries at scale, and where their failure modes are exposed before they ever deploy. We work as a neutral partner to defence manufacturers and governments. Founded in London in January 2026, we’ve raised $100M to date. Our $70M Series A, at a $450M valuation, was led by Northzone alongside Lakestar, Lux Capital and XYZ, with backing from former Sequoia Capital head Roelof Botha. It was also the first joint investment by the UK Government’s Sovereign AI Fund and the National Security Strategic Investment Fund. Between them, our founders have helped build one of the defining defence-tech companies of the last decade, and started an aerospace company from scratch. Around them is a founding team hand-picked from Europe’s best engineers, each at the top of their field, and brought together to build this. We’re scaling fast across our offices in London and Berlin. The role As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll be the technical bridge between Agon’s AI development environment and our customers’ real-world model development workflows. You’ll work in small teams and own end-to-end delivery of high-stakes projects. You’ll embed with customers, working in their models, data and pipelines, and integrate our platform so their teams can build, simulate and validate AI systems at scale. Every FDE works directly with customers, writes production software and builds a strong understanding of the defence domain. If you’re strong in software and with customers but new to defence, we’d still like to hear from you. This role is based in London, with regular travel to customer sites and our Berlin office, mainly within Europe. What you’ll do Deploy and integrate: work directly with customers to deploy and operationalise Agon’s AI development environment, connecting it to their models, data sources and pipelines. Solve broad technical problems: tackle software engineering, simulation and synthetic-data pipelines, ML workflows, cloud infrastructure and system deployment. Bridge systems: connect customer-built systems to Agon’s platform to deliver real value quickly. Build repeatable approaches: design architectures and ways of working that make customer projects consistent and scalable. Own outcomes: drive projects to completion, adapting as requirements and priorities change. Be the voice of the customer: feed real-world friction and needs back to our product and engineering teams. The right attitude: your references would describe you as low-ego, highly motivated, thoughtfully opinionated, a strong communicator and a curious listener. Willingness to travel: to work on site with customers and between our offices, mainly within Europe. Pay: salary at the 90th percentile of the companies we compete with, benchmarked by role, level and location. Equity: every permanent employee holds options. jobs.jd: At Parallel Domain, we believe that autonomous systems – from self-driving cars to contactless delivery drones – have the opportunity to drastically improve the quality of life for billions of people. That is why we love what we do: enabling our customers to develop their technology safely using the Parallel Domain data generation platform. Our platform revolutionizes the way our customers generate sensor data for AI development. We're looking for people like you to join us in pushing the boundaries of artificial intelligence and synthetic data. About the role Before any physical AI system is trusted in the real world, it has to prove itself in ours. Parallel Domain turns real captured drives into faithful digital replicas — geometry, appearance and motion that perception stacks are trained and validated against. We are hiring a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to push our feed-forward reconstruction stack forward — from static 3D toward full 4D scenes over time. You will join a small, deep team where your technical judgment carries real weight from day one, and your work will ship in a pipeline customers depend on. What You'll Do Advance our feed-forward reconstruction models . Improve how we predict geometry, camera pose and appearance from real capture with transformer-based models, and extend it from static scenes to dynamic 4D. Train at scale . Run multi-node GPU training on large multi-view and video datasets, and decide what to scale, what to ablate and when a result is real. Define what "good" means . Build evaluation the team trusts for reconstruction quality, temporal consistency and geometric accuracy. Explore stronger priors . Investigate where generative models, such as pre-trained video diffusion, can help fill gaps the capture did not see. Land research in the product . Work with the pipeline engineers to get results into production, and care whether they hold up there. Track the field . This area moves monthly; form a view on where it is heading and argue for it. What we're looking for Hands-on feed-forward reconstruction experience . You have built or trained feedforward 3D reconstruction models (for example in the lineage of DUSt3R, VGGT, π³ or D4RT), and you know where they work and where they break. A track record of models others relied on . We weight demonstrated depth over years served : a recent PhD with the right focus and an experienced research engineer are both credible here. Large-scale trainin g. Practical experience with multi-node, multi-GPU training and telling a promising run from a stalled one early. Strong PyTorch skills in a large shared codebase with real build and CI. Research judgment . You turn an ambiguous direction into experiments that resolve something, and change your mind when the numbers say so. Clear communication with researchers, pipeline engineers and leadership alike. Strong pluses These are listed in order of how much they matter to us. Feed-forward Gaussian prediction . Experience predicting 3D Gaussians directly from images in a single pass, rather than fitting them per scene. Top-tier publications in feed-forward reconstruction . First-author or significant work at CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR or SIGGRAPH in this area. Video diffusion models . Familiarity with diffusion or flow-matching video models, especially camera-conditioned generation. Dynamic scenes . Work on dynamic reconstruction, scene flow or temporal consistency. Real-world capture . Experience with automotive, robotics or drone data and its mess: imperfect calibration, motion blur, poses you cannot trust. Making big models fast, or open-source contributions to widely used reconstruction libraries. Why join Parallel Domain? We are assembling a team of creative, talented visionaries seeking to build a new technology that will change the world. You will be able to learn, build, and scale our team and technology in a collaborative, creative culture that values every team member. To attract and inspire the right talent, we offer: • Competitive compensation (range will be openly discussed early in our interview process) • Employer-paid supplemental medical, mental health, dental, and vision benefits. • Flexible paid vacation, sick time, winter shutdown, and 11+ holidays per year • Paid parental leave • Equipment budget to optimize your setup • Annual learning and development stipend Parallel Domain celebrates diversity and is committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment for all our people. jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, AWS Elemental
jobs.jd: AWS Elemental builds media services used by broadcasters, streaming platforms, and sports leagues to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video. Elemental Inference is the applied machine learning team within that organization. We develop models that understand and transform live and file-based video, producing capabilities such as intelligent reframing, highlight detection, video enhancement, and contextual metadata for advertising and content discovery. Our work reaches customers through the same media workflows that carry major live events, always-on channels, and large on-demand libraries. As a Senior Applied Scientist, you will develop new machine learning approaches and carry the strongest ideas into production. Current work spans multimodal video, audio, and language models; spatial and temporal understanding; active-speaker and point-of-interest detection; scene retrieval; video super-resolution; and learned methods for improving compression. These problems rarely have a single accepted metric or a ready-made dataset. You will help define the task itself, determine what evidence is needed, and build evaluation methods that reflect the experience of people watching and working with the resulting video. This role combines applied research with the practical demands of a real-time media service. You will design datasets and objectives, train models at scale, run controlled comparisons, and investigate failures. You will also work closely with engineers to export, optimize, and deploy those models. A result is not finished when it performs well in a notebook. It must preserve its quality after conversion, fit within GPU memory, meet latency and throughput targets, handle the temporal behavior of live video, and operate at a cost customers can sustain. You will be a technical leader on the team as well as an individual contributor. The role calls for someone who can take an ambiguous customer problem, separate the scientific questions from the engineering constraints, and lead a team toward a defensible answer. You will review experiments and models, mentor other scientists and engineers, and improve the shared methods the team uses for training and evaluation. Strong judgment matters here. So does the ability to explain a complicated result clearly, including its limitations, to people from several disciplines. We welcome candidates with deep experience in computer vision, multimodal learning, video processing, or related areas. Direct media experience is valuable but not required. A scientist who has solved difficult problems in another field, understands how to test ideas rigorously, and wants to learn the video domain can also succeed in this role. Key job responsibilities Lead the formulation of ambiguous video problems into research plans with clear datasets, objectives, baselines, evaluation protocols, and production acceptance criteria. Develop models for multimodal video understanding and generation, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression. Develop models for multimodal video understanding and description, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression. Build evaluations that measure the behavior customers will see. Depending on the problem, this may include task accuracy, factual support, temporal localization, retrieval quality, perceptual video quality, rate-distortion performance, or human review. Take models from research code to production-ready artifacts. Partner with engineers on model export, reduced-precision inference, quantization, numerical parity, accelerator-specific optimization, and integration with serving systems and video pipelines. Balance model quality against latency, throughput, GPU memory, context limits, and operating cost. Diagnose problems across training stability, data quality, precision, compilation, serving, and live temporal behavior. Build reusable mechanisms for dataset management, experimentation, model comparison, regression detection, and performance measurement rather than solving each research problem in isolation. Review scientific work and production code. Identify weak comparisons, data leakage, unsupported conclusions, untested edge cases, and operational risks before they reach customers. Work with product managers, software engineers, and other scientists to make scope and design decisions. Use evidence to resolve disagreement and communicate what is known, what remains uncertain, and what further work is worth doing. Mentor scientists and engineers in experimental design, machine learning methods, video evaluation, and production ML practices. Contribute applied research through internal technical reports, patents, and publications at appropriate conferences or workshops. About the team AWS Elemental provides a portfolio of cloud media services built to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video at global scale. Our technology supports some of the world's largest live broadcasts as well as 24/7 channels and on-demand content. The broader organization brings together expertise in video coding, image processing, distributed systems, advertising, and the operational demands of professional media. Elemental Inference applies machine learning across that video pipeline. The team works on video understanding and enhancement, contextual metadata, smart composition, event detection, retrieval, and compression. Some projects use large multimodal models that combine video, audio, and language. Others use specialized temporal or spatial models designed for a narrow task and a strict real-time budget. We choose the approach that fits the customer problem rather than forcing every problem into the same model family. Scientists on the team own more than model architecture. They build and govern datasets, develop annotation methods, train on distributed GPU infrastructure, and create evaluations

jobs.title: Research Engineer/Research Scientist- Post Training, Model Experience
jobs.jd: About the Team The Post Training team is responsible for training and improving pre-trained models to be deployed into ChatGPT, the API, and potential future products. In the Model Experience team, we shape the default character and behavior of ChatGPT: how the model communicates, responds to users, uses its capabilities, and behaves across different contexts and languages. Our goal is to make every interaction with ChatGPT thoughtful, helpful, and trustworthy. We take an opinionated view of what good human–AI interaction should look like, then turn that vision into real model behavior through human data, evaluations, reward models, and post-training. Our work sits at the intersection of research, product, and model design. We partner closely with teams across OpenAI to conduct research and ensure our models are thoughtful, safe, reliable to serve millions of users. jobs.title: Advisory Solution Consultant - CRM & Agentic AI
jobs.jd: As an Advisory Solution Consultant - CRM & Agentic AI for the Public Sector in Germany , you are the technical face of a fundamentally different way of selling. Rather than leading with slideware and scripted demos, you embed alongside the customer, run deep Discovery to isolate one high-value problem, and then prove value in the open — building a working Proof of Value (POV) on the customer’s own data using our Agentic workflow capabilities. You partner with Sales, Product Management, and Executive Leadership to turn a single, well-chosen use case into undeniable, data-backed proof that earns the next phase of the relationship. This role blends the consultative instincts of a Sr. Advisory Solution Consultant with the hands-on, build-it-in-the-field engineering of a forward-deployed engineer: someone who works inside the customer’s own environment, configuring and proving solutions on their live data rather than presenting finished products from the outside. The Embedded Approach The Advisory Solution Consultant inverts the traditional pre-sales motion. Product demonstration is deliberately minimal — just enough to establish credibility and unlock the real work. The center of gravity is the POV: a short, focused cycle where we get access to a slice of the customer’s data, stand up an Agentic workflow against a problem they genuinely care about, and let the outcome speak for itself. Your job is to earn the right to that POV through rigorous Discovery, then deliver it as an embedded engineer, not a presenter. What You’ll Do As the Advisory Solution Consultant, you will lead a Discovery-first, POV-centric engagement model — using your technical depth and Agentic workflow expertise to convert customer data into proven outcomes, while supporting quarterly and annual sales objectives for your region. Key responsibilities include: Partner with Sales as the embedded technical lead — someone who wins on proof, not presentation — to drive transformational CRM opportunities. Lead rigorous Discovery to isolate a single, high-value problem worth solving, mapping the customer’s data, systems, and desired outcome before any product is shown. Keep product demonstration minimal and purposeful — use it only to establish credibility and to set up the POV, never as a substitute for proving value on real data. Secure and scope a POV: earn customer sponsorship to engage in a hands-on cycle where we use their data to solve the identified problem with our Agentic workflow capabilities. Build and deliver the POV as an embedded engineer — configuring Agentic workflows against the customer’s environment and producing measurable, data-backed results. Translate POV outcomes into an executive value narrative that quantifies impact and defines the path from a single proven use case to enterprise-wide adoption. Collaborate with Product Management using field and POV learnings to shape Agentic workflow, integration (e.g. ERP), and AI-driven capabilities that address real enterprise needs. Ensure every Discovery and POV engagement aligns with regional data privacy laws, security expectations, and enterprise compliance standards for handling customer data. Codify reusable POV assets, Discovery frameworks, and Agentic workflow patterns so the embedded POV motion scales across the team. Represent the company at enterprise events, technology forums, and leadership summits as a credible, hands-on technical voice for the embedded POV approach. What We’re Looking For To succeed in this role, you should bring: Builder Mindset: A builder’s instinct — comfortable getting hands on with a customer’s data and environment to prove value directly, rather than relying on canned demonstrations. POV-Centric Selling: Proven ability to scope, sell, and deliver Proof-of-Value engagements that convert a single problem into quantified, data-backed outcomes. Discovery Rigor: Exceptional discovery skills to quickly isolate the one problem worth solving and secure customer commitment to a POV. Agentic & AI Fluency: Deep, practical understanding of Agentic workflows and AI-driven automation, and how to apply them to CRM problems on live customer data. CRM Expertise: Deep hands-on experience in CRM and customer experience, with strong knowledge of service, sales, lead & opportunity management. Enterprise Experience: Proven track record engaging large organizations and earning executive sponsorship for hands-on, data-driven engagements. Communication Skills: Exceptional ability to translate technical POV results into clear, business-oriented value stories for senior enterprise stakeholders. Collaboration: Proven ability to work effectively in cross-functional, global teams spanning Sales, Product, and delivery. Language: fluency in English and German Qualifications Demonstrated experience building or delivering POVs, prototypes, or hands-on technical engagements — a hands-on track record of proving value on real customer data, not just presenting it. Hands-on experience applying AI and Agentic workflow capabilities to solve business problems — automating workflows, orchestrating AI agents, and analyzing AI-driven outcomes within CRM or adjacent enterprise contexts. 10+ years of pre-sales solution consulting or sales engineering experience, with a clear shift toward Discovery-led, proof-based selling. Experience of selling into Federal / Public Sector organisations Proficiency with the ServiceNow platform or strong technical expertise with cloud software solutions. Experience working collaboratively with product management, product marketing, partners, and professional services. Track record of working with a Sales counterpart to promote execution excellence and advance transformational opportunities.
